title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on Gauss–Manin connections and the Cartier operation. The surrounding pages ask: for X→S over a base S of finite type over Z, if a closed 1-form behaves well under the Cartier operator at almost every closed point (p-curvature-type condition), must it be 'logarithmic' globally? Here the cancelled opening restricts to X→S proper, where the relevant forms are ω ∈ f_*(Z^1_{X/S}) = Ker(f_*Ω^1 → f_*Ω^2).

1. Translation for abelian schemes. Grothendieck takes X→S abelian, introduces the dual abelian scheme A and its universal vector extension E: 0 → V → E → A → 0, with V = f_*Ω^1_{X/S} the vector part. A margin note says the translation also works more generally for X→S proper and smooth. Points of E are rank-one line bundles in Pic^0 with integrable connection, so Lie E = H^1_dR. A section of V is a closed global 1-form ω, i.e. the connection d+ω on the trivial bundle.

2. Question (c). The rank-one problem becomes a diophantine statement. Let ω ∈ E(S) with, for every closed s of residue characteristic p, ω(s) ∈ pE_s(k(s)) (equivalently ω(s) lies in the image of Verschiebung). Is the image of ω in A(S) of finite order?
- Part (a): the image in A is torsion.
- Part (b): if moreover ω lies in V, then ω = 0.

3. Why the condition is the right one. Take k = k(s) finite and p ∤ #A(k). Then E(k) splits canonically as k^g × A(k), and pE(k) is the A(k)-factor. So 'ω(s) ∈ pE_s' says the vector component vanishes, which is a p-curvature-zero condition. This is the rank-one Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture expressed as a reduction/divisibility statement on the universal vector extension.

4. Question (d), a generalisation to arbitrary group schemes. Let S be integral, of finite type and dominant over Spec Z, E a group scheme of finite type over S (not necessarily connected), and ω ∈ E(S). Suppose that for every closed s, ω(s) lies in a subgroup of E_s that is connected and proper (resp. of zero unipotent/abelian rank, resp. affine, resp. unipotent). Does ω(η) at the generic point then lie in a subgroup of the same type? The page breaks off here.

5. The next page adds (e): ω ∈ A(S), A abelian, with ω(s) coming from A^{(p^n)} via Verschiebung for all s; is ω torsion?

Purpose: to reduce the p-curvature/Cartier question for proper smooth families to a local-global question on points of commutative group schemes.
errors: The condition ω(s) ∈ pE_s is nearly vacuous on the abelian part. For most closed points p ∤ #A(k(s)), so the content lies entirely in the vector component. Grothendieck does not remark on this, though it is consistent with the p-curvature interpretation.

Question (d) is stated loosely and the 'resp.' cases are unfinished. For instance, for E = G_m the 'proper connected subgroup' condition forces ω(s) = 1, which makes those cases trivial. The intended precise hypotheses (e.g. commutativity, as on the previous page) are not fixed.

ideas.what: Reformulating the rank-one Cartier/p-curvature question for closed 1-forms on abelian (or proper smooth) schemes as a question about sections of the universal vector extension of the dual abelian scheme whose reductions are p-divisible
ideas.modern_name: Rank-one Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture via the universal vector extension E(A^∨) = Pic^♮
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjecture: Grothendieck (via Katz 1972). Universal vector extension: Grothendieck / Mazur–Messing 1974. Rank-one case: Chudnovsky (curves), Bost (2001), André (2004)
ideas.where_published: Universal extension in Grothendieck's 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux' (ICM 1970) and Mazur–Messing LNM 370. The p-curvature conjecture in Katz, Invent. Math. 1972

ideas.what: Splitting of the problem into (a) torsion of the image in A and (b) vanishing of a vector (1-form) section satisfying the p-divisibility condition
ideas.modern_name: Torsion of the line bundle versus triviality of a closed-form connection with vanishing p-curvature

ideas.what: Question (d): local-global principle for whether a section of a group scheme over an arithmetic base lies in a connected subgroup of a given type (proper / affine / unipotent), tested at all closed fibres
ideas.modern_name: Reduction / local-global problems for points of algebraic groups (cf. support problem, detecting linear dependence by reductions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Later work: Corrales-Rodrigáñez–Schoof 1997, Larsen, Pink 2004, Gajda–Górnisiewicz, Banaszak, Weston (mostly ℓ ≠ p, abelian varieties)

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses a general local-global question for arbitrary group schemes of finite type over arithmetic bases. If the reductions at all closed points lie in connected subgroups that are proper (resp. affine, resp. unipotent, resp. of zero unipotent rank), must the generic point lie in a subgroup of the same type? Unlike the later 'reduction of Mordell–Weil' literature, this uses residue-characteristic phenomena (unipotent subgroups, Verschiebung), and that variant seems not systematically studied.
missed.quote: Supposons que pour tout pt fermé s∈S, ω(s) appartienne à un sous-groupe de E_s qui est connexe propre sur k(s) [resp. connexe ... affine, resp. connexe unipotent] alors ω(y) appartient à un ss-groupe de E_y qui est propre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a characteristic-p-sensitive local-global principle for group schemes. It would generalise the rank-one p-curvature theorem (Bost/André) to non-commutative and mixed extensions, and it is distinct from the ℓ-adic support problems studied since the 1990s.

missed.claim: An explicit early (c. 1972) formulation of the rank-one p-curvature conjecture as a diophantine statement on the universal vector extension: p-divisibility of reductions implies torsion. This is the viewpoint later exploited by Bost and André via formal subgroups of E^♮.
missed.quote: Soit ω une section de E sur S, supposons que pour tout pt fermé s∈S, ω(s)∈ ... (=pE_s) ... Alors l'image section ω dans Γ(S,A_S) est-elle d'ordre fini ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it shows Grothendieck himself linked the p-curvature conjecture to arithmetic of universal vector extensions. Mathematically, this case is now settled (Bost 2001, André 2004).

deep.surprise_reason: The translation of the rank-one p-curvature problem into p-divisibility of reductions of sections of the universal vector extension is natural and was later carried out and solved (Chudnovsky, Bost, André). Seeing it explicitly in Grothendieck's hand around 1972 is a notable historical detail. The broader group-scheme question (d) is an unfinished and somewhat unusual characteristic-p local-global question.
transcription_corrections: '[NB. ceci signifie que l'image de ω ...' should read '[NB. a) signifie que l'image de ω dans Γ(S,A_S) est d'ordre fini, b) signifie que si ...'.
'[?] extension de schéma abélien dual A, et la extension vectorielle universelle E' is probably 'si on introduit le schéma abélien dual A, et l'extension vectorielle universelle E'.
Margin likely reads 'cette traduction marche aussi, plus généralement, si X→S propre et lisse'.
'ω(s) ∈ A_s^{φ(p(s))} (=pE_s)' is probably 'ω(s) ∈ E_s^{(p)}' or the image of Verschiebung, glossed as pE_s. The letter A there is doubtful.
In d), '[-A-] E un schéma en groupes' is probably 'soit E un schéma en groupes de tf. (non nécessairement connexe)'.
'[resp. connexe de rang unipotent nul ...]' might be 'de rang abélien nul'; uncertain.
